key_insight: Extending high-rate many-hypercube quantum codes from qubits to prime-dimensional qudits improves error correction, with higher local dimension yielding markedly better threshold performance.
engineering_relevance: Qudit-based fault-tolerant architectures could reduce logical error rates at fixed code rate, making scalable quantum computing more efficient than qubit-only designs.
method: Constructed level-2 and level-3 qudit MHC codes with parameters [[6^2,4^2,2^2]]_q and [[6^3,4^3,2^3]]_q.
Generalized the level-by-level minimum-distance (LLMD) decoder to qudit codes.
Evaluated code-capacity performance under a qudit X-error model for prime dimensions up to q=13.
evidence_signal: The reported error threshold rises monotonically with q, reaching 10.0% at q=13 versus 5.1% for qubits, and the authors also observe a strong waterfall regime at larger q.
watch_item: The reported gains are shown for a qudit X-error model and code-capacity setting, so hardware implementation and broader noise models may reduce the practical advantage.
paper_title: High-Rate Concatenated Quantum Error-Correcting Codes for Qudits
